summary: DHSC to extend US tech firm’s contract for two more years to allow time to line up British companies to replace itMinisters will end the NHS’s contract with the controversial tech firm Palantir – but not until 2029, to allow time to line up British companies to replace it.The Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) has decided to extend Palantir’s contract to provide the federated data platform (FDP) – the software that links different healthcare providers – for two more years rather than exercise a break clause that would have let them axe it next spring.

stories.title: How Milburn won over Labour on tackling rising youth unemployment

stories.title: Saudi Arabia strategy challenged by anti-Houthi forces in Yemen
summary: Accusations of incompetence follow retreat of Riyadh-backed forces in effort to relieve siege of Taiz and protect Aden Saudi Arabia has been accused by anti-Houthi forces over its military strategy after its Yemeni allies withdrew troops from the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait and pulled back forces from parts of Marib in the central part of the country.The Saudi-backed government explained the repositioning by saying the strategic priority was to break the attritional siege on Taiz, Yemen’s third city, and to protect Aden, the southern port city in which the Saudi-backed and UN-recognised government is now based.

summary: Lizbeth Vargas Andrade, 23, was taken down by officers and arrested on her stomach during a protest, her attorney saysUS Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents pepper-sprayed a pregnant US citizen and threw her to the ground during a protest in California on Sunday, according to her family’s attorney, who shared footage of the incident.Lizbeth Vargas Andrade, 23, was filming and protesting the presence of several ICE officers outside the Stanislaus county jail in Modesto, in California’s central valley, before she was taken down by officers and arrested on her stomach during a chaotic encounter.
